intro: Eight weeks of the trade, kept the way a ledger should be kept — dated, sourced, and in one place. New entries are added at the top each week; the quarter's running numbers live in the Almanac below.

entries.h: China's jewellery counter is 39.47% above the Shanghai exchange price, and the gap has widened since 8 August
entries.t: The Shanghai Gold Exchange closed its Au99.99 contract at 940.72 yuan a gram on 14 August 2026, from an opening of 955.00 and a session low of 933.01, on volume of 3,886.14 kilogrammes; the deferred Au(T+D) contract closed at 940.44 on 41,646 kilogrammes. Those figures are taken from the exchange's own published daily quotations rather than from an aggregator. On the same day Chow Tai Fook listed 24-carat jewellery at 1,312 yuan a gram, a figure carried identically by two independent Chinese price aggregators, jinjia.com.cn and cngold. Dividing the counter price by the exchange price, this desk's arithmetic, puts the counter 39.47% above the exchange, a gap of 371.28 yuan on every gram. This paper published the same pair on 9 August 2026 at 938 yuan on the exchange and 1,286 at the counter, a gap of 348 yuan and a markup of 37.10%. Six days later the exchange has moved 2.72 yuan, or 0.29%, and the counter has moved 26 yuan, or 2.02%, so the gap has widened by 23.28 yuan a gram rather than closing. Today both legs fell: the exchange closed 8.52 yuan, or 0.90%, below its 13 August close of 949.24, while the counter came off 28 yuan, or 2.09%, from 1,340, roughly two and a third times as fast, narrowing the premium from 41.17% on one aggregator's 13 August counter price, or 40.01% on the other's, to 39.47%. Across the sessions the aggregator series records this month the Chow Tai Fook price has gone 1,231, 1,240, 1,297, 1,286, 1,308, 1,308, 1,336, 1,329, 1,340 and 1,312. On the readings this desk can verify, the Chinese jewellery markup has run between 37.10% and 41.17% in August. Two divergences between outside sources are disclosed: one aggregator's series carries 1,286 against 7 August rather than the 8 August this paper published it under, and the two aggregators disagree about 13 August by 11 yuan, at 1,340 and 1,329. Separately, the Bank of China's market note of 13 August put Shanghai spot gold up 0.96% at 955.75 yuan a gram against the exchange's own close of 949.24 for that date; the exchange's own figure is used here. A listed counter price is an asking price rather than a transacted one, and workmanship charges, store discounts and buy-back terms sit outside both numbers.
entries.s: Shanghai Gold Exchange daily quotations (14 August 2026) / jinjia.com.cn / cngold / Bank of China market note (13 August 2026) / Carat Capital arithmetic and archive

entries.h: All four metals written back on one board, ending a two-session platinum hold at $1,725.00
entries.t: On 14 August 2026 Kitco's live board at 06:00 New York time read gold at $4,356.20 an ounce, silver at $64.77, platinum at $1,725.00 and palladium at $1,297.00. Under the one-price rule the Editor wrote all four readings back over caratwire's 04:59 marks, with the new timestamp and the source named on the tape before the edition built. Measured against this paper's own marks of record 24 hours earlier, gold fell $27.90 or 0.64%, silver rose $0.25 or 0.39%, platinum rose $15.00 or 0.88% and palladium fell $22.00 or 1.67%. Gold and silver were cross-checked the same morning against TradingEconomics at $4,356.79 and $64.89, differences of 0.01% and 0.19%. The gold-to-silver ratio, this desk's division of its own published gold mark by its own published silver mark on the same board at the same minute, narrowed to 67.26 from 67.95. Platinum had been held twice: on 12 August 2026 because Kitco's cell was stale, and on 13 August 2026 because Kitco's live cell sat $14.60 below TradingEconomics and JM Bullion, which agreed with each other to within 50 cents. At 04:59 on 14 August the tape desk found the same shape a third time, with Kitco $13.30 below TradingEconomics, and held again. At 06:00 the gap was $12.70 against TradingEconomics at $1,737.70 and $14.90 against JM Bullion at $1,739.90, with those two pages agreeing to $2.20, or 0.13%. This desk's judgement is that a gap recurring at the same size and sign across three consecutive sessions is a basis difference between outside pages rather than an unreadable market, and that continuing to hold had produced a mark two sessions old and 1.62% below where two other pages put the metal. Platinum is therefore written back on Kitco, the board that carries every other mark on this tape, and palladium with it at Kitco's $1,297.00 bid; JM Bullion read palladium at $1,336.71 at 06:01, $39.71 or 3.06% higher, disclosed as the other side of a thin spread. At 31.1035 grams to the troy ounce the four marks work out at $140.05 a gram of fine gold, $2.08 of fine silver, $55.46 of fine platinum and $41.70 of fine palladium, all this desk's arithmetic.
entries.s: Kitco / TradingEconomics / JM Bullion / Carat Capital tape and arithmetic

entries.h: Gold ETFs took in $3bn in July; Europe supplied $2bn of it and North America $71mn
entries.t: The World Gold Council reported on 6 August 2026, under the title Europe's golden heatwave, that global physically backed gold exchange-traded funds took in US$3 billion in July 2026, reversing two consecutive months of outflows. Collective holdings rose 23 tonnes to 4,068 tonnes and assets under management rose 1% to US$530 billion. Holdings remain 108 tonnes, or 2.59%, below the record of 4,176 tonnes set on 27 February 2026, that subtraction being this desk's. By region, Europe took US$2 billion, of which the United Kingdom contributed US$875 million and Switzerland US$657 million; Asia took US$616 million, with China the strongest contributor and Japan in outflow; North America took US$71 million; and other regions, chiefly Australia and South Africa, took US$140 million. Britain and Switzerland together raised US$1,532 million against US$827 million from Asia, North America and all other regions combined, a ratio of 1.85 to one, and North America supplied 2.5% of the named regional total; both figures are this desk's arithmetic. The named regional components sum to US$2,827 million against a rounded headline of US$3 billion because every component is rounded, a difference this desk states rather than reconciles. Year to date, global gold ETF inflows amounted to US$11 billion, equivalent to a 39-tonne increase in holdings. Average daily trading volumes across the gold market fell 3.5% to US$356 billion in the month and over-the-counter volumes fell 3.4% to US$205 billion. This paper has previously reported global jewellery demand of 278 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026, the smallest since the pandemic, on 31 July 2026; Indian jewellery demand of 75.1 tonnes, down 15% by weight, on the same day; China's gold jewellery consumption at its lowest since 2004, on 3 August 2026; and China's heaviest month of bullion buying since 2023, on 9 August 2026. This is the first coverage of the World Gold Council's monthly ETF flows series in this paper's archive, and the report is eight days old as it prints.
entries.s: World Gold Council, Gold ETF Flows: July 2026 (6 August 2026) / Carat Capital arithmetic and archive

entries.h: Sarine's first-half deficit widened 21-fold on a revenue decline of about $0.9 million
entries.t: Sarine Technologies reported results for the six months ended 30 June 2026 on 11 August 2026. Revenue was $14.4 million, down 6% on the first half of 2025, and the group recorded a net loss of $3.5 million against a net loss of $166,000 in the comparable half. No dividend was declared. Dividing one deficit by the other gives 21.1 times, this desk's arithmetic on the two published figures. Taking 6% off the published revenue implies revenue of roughly $15.3 million in the first half of 2025, which puts the revenue decline at about $0.9 million against a deficit that widened by $3.334 million, or approximately three and a half times the fall in the top line; those three figures are this desk's arithmetic on rounded published figures and are published by no source. The company attributes the wider loss to higher operating expenses, driven by a weaker US dollar against the Israeli shekel, and to reduced natural-diamond processing volumes in the face of lab-grown competition. Against that, revenue from GCAL grading rose more than 50% in the half, revenue from the MVP rough-planning service more than doubled, and Kitov.ai, the industrial-inspection associate in which Sarine holds 33%, booked $1.5 million of revenue and also more than doubled. The company's own framing is that a 6% revenue decline is modest relative to a significantly greater contraction in rough diamond supply. Sarine sells the scanning, planning and grading equipment and services that stones pass through on the way to a polished parcel, so its revenue tracks stones processed rather than stones sold at retail. This paper published global rough production down 8% to 98.8 million carats in 2025 on 27 July 2026, and Lucara Diamond selling 24% fewer carats in its second quarter on 12 August 2026. This is the first coverage of Sarine Technologies in this paper's archive.
entries.s: Rapaport (11 August 2026) / Minichart (11 August 2026) / Carat Capital arithmetic and archive

entries.h: Titan says natural-diamond pricing has stabilised, on a 43% jewellery quarter
entries.t: In remarks published on 12 August 2026, Arun Narayan, chief executive of Titan's jewellery business, said the company has seen more stability in the pricing of both solitaires and small diamonds, and Ajoy Chawla, Titan's managing director, said that at the market level natural-diamond pricing has stabilized and that the lab-grown-versus-natural narrative has faded from the conversation. Titan reported a resurgence in diamond-jewellery buying in the fourth quarter of its fiscal 2026 and into the first quarter of fiscal 2027, with demand strengthening through the April-to-June period. Titan's consolidated income for the three months to 30 June 2026 was Rs 20,753 crore, up 40% year on year, with profit before tax of Rs 2,429 crore, up 64%, at a margin of 11.7%. The jewellery division recorded Rs 18,253 crore, up 43% excluding bullion and digital gold, at an EBIT of Rs 2,360 crore and a margin of 12.9%. Watches and wearables recorded Rs 1,543 crore, up 21%, at an EBIT margin of 19.1%. The group added a net 77 stores in the quarter to reach 3,680 worldwide as at June 2026. This paper published the same quarter on 28 July 2026 from the company's own business update at approximately 41% revenue growth and 39% for jewellery; the 43% figure excludes bullion and digital gold and is a different basis rather than a revision. A third basis circulating in secondary coverage, revenue from operations of Rs 21,356 crore and growth of 29.25% against Rs 16,523 crore, is internally consistent on its own terms and does not agree with the 40% consolidated-income headline; the divergence is disclosed rather than resolved. Titan is a retailer of natural diamonds and the statement is made by an interested party on its own earnings call. This paper reported Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter of 2026 even as its value rose.
entries.s: Rapaport (12 August 2026) / afaqs (8 August 2026) / Sahi (7 August 2026) / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Kiran Gems USA says 0.30 to 0.70-carat goods are selling at 1990s prices
entries.t: On Rapaport's Heard on the Street, published 12 August 2026, Senil Lakhani, president of Kiran Gems USA, said that diamonds below one carat and up to 1.5 carats are less expensive than ever before and are selling at prices from the 1990s and early 2000s. He identified the 0.30, 0.40, 0.50 and 0.70-carat range as the bread and butter for America and placed the relevant price points at $1,000, $2,000 and $5,000 rather than at the half-million and million-dollar level. Kiran Gems is one of the largest diamond manufacturers in the world. This paper has reported the same goods from the index side through August: RapNet monthly moves for July had 0.30-carat goods up 1.6% and 0.50-carat goods up 1.8% against a flat one-carat index, published here on 4 August 2026, and the colour split inside that flat month had K to M goods averaging 1.7% against 0.1% for D to F and G to J colours in IF to VVS and VS clarity, published here on 12 August 2026. Those figures are directions for a single month; the characterisation of a 1990s price level is a level, and no index reachable by this desk publishes a 1999 comparison for 0.30 to 0.70-carat goods, so the level claim is reported as a named executive's characterisation of his own market and not as a price. On the same panel, Jeff Angel, head buyer at RDI Diamonds, said he can locate a diamond of traceable Botswana origin in about five minutes and recently filled a million-dollar order in which every stone was required to come from Botswana. Other participants in the episode included Ari Jain of House of Diamonds, Angelo Palmieri of GCAL by Sarine and Kerri Lavine of Diamanti NYC, moderated by Heather Chambers.
entries.s: Rapaport Heard on the Street (12 August 2026) / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Lucara's realised price a carat rose 23.7% while both its sales channels cut prices
entries.t: Lucara Diamond released its second-quarter 2026 results on 7 August 2026. The company sold 58,553 carats from its Karowe mine in Botswana during the quarter, against 77,167 carats in the second quarter of 2025, and recorded revenue of $41.0 million against $43.7 million, a fall of 6% on a 24% fall in carats sold. Dividing the published revenue by the published carats gives a realised price of $700.22 a carat for the quarter against $566.30 a year earlier, a rise of 23.7%; on the first half the same division gives $454.10 a carat against $493.21, a fall of 7.9%. All four of those per-carat figures are this desk's arithmetic and are published by no source. The company's own commentary states that average prices per carat declined across both channels, with tender prices falling 5% and Clara prices falling 17%, which it attributes to continued pricing pressure on mid-range and lower-grade stones. The whole of the realisation gain is therefore composition rather than price. It is not a function of more large stones reaching the surface either: specials, the stones above 10.8 carats, were recovered at 176 in the quarter against 242 a year earlier. Second-quarter net income was $15.6 million against $12.5 million; first-half net income was $1.0 million against $12.4 million, a fall of 92%, which implies a first-quarter loss of roughly $14.6 million by subtraction, this desk's arithmetic. The plant processed 761,848 tonnes of ore and recovered 90,082 carats at a grade of 10.9 carats per hundred tonnes, of which 6,973 carats came from tailings, at an operating cost of $23.76 a tonne, down 11% from $26.76. Full-year guidance was maintained at revenue of $100 million to $130 million, carats recovered and carats sold each at 340,000 to 360,000, ore processed at 2.6 to 2.9 million tonnes, operating costs of $27.50 to $31.00 a tonne, underground project capital of up to $110 million and sustaining capital of up to $11.5 million. Against $62.8 million of first-half revenue and 138,297 carats sold, that requires $37.2 million to $67.2 million and 201,703 to 221,703 carats in the second half, or 59% to 62% of the year's sales after the halfway point, all derived by this desk. Cash stood at $243.6 million at 30 June against bonds payable of $342.8 million with nothing drawn on the working capital or project facilities. The Karowe underground project has $275.9 million of completion cost remaining including contingency, with full production expected in the first half of 2028 and open-pit mining on track to conclude in the fourth quarter of 2026; in July 2026 the Botswana Department of Mines licensed the 15-person auxiliary winder and the 105-person man and material winder on the production shaft.
entries.s: Lucara Diamond Q2 2026 results via CNW (7 August 2026) / Rapaport / Carat Capital arithmetic

entries.h: Signet gives Zales and Banter to Mattel's former global head of dolls
entries.t: Signet Jewelers announced on 11 August 2026, from Hamilton, Bermuda, that Jamie Cygielman has been named president of Zales and Banter, effective 24 August 2026. She will be based in Dallas and reports directly to J.K. Symancyk, Signet's chief executive officer. She joins from Mattel, where she was global head of dolls, a portfolio she reached after serving as general manager and president of American Girl and which she later widened to include Barbie. The same release named Pam Cloud president of Blue Nile with effect from 10 August 2026, based in New York City; Cloud spent more than 25 years at Tiffany and Co., latterly as senior vice president and chief merchandising officer, an appointment this paper reported on 6 August 2026. Two of Signet's four brand families therefore changed president within eight days, and the two appointments are different in kind: one seat was filled from inside the jewellery trade and the other from a toy company. Under Grow Brand Love, the strategy launched by Symancyk in March 2025, Signet is organised into four customer families: Kay and Peoples for core milestone and romantic gifting, Zales and Banter for style and trend, Jared for inspired luxury, and Blue Nile for luxury. The stated aim of the strategy is to have the company's chains operate as brands rather than as retail banners and to grow share in adjacent categories, notably everyday jewellery. Gold spot stood at $4,415.20 an ounce on this paper's tape the same morning, up 0.97% on the paper's previous mark of record and up 6.2% on the $4,158.30 the tape carried on 5 August 2026.
entries.s: Signet Jewelers (11 August 2026) / Forbes / Rapaport / Carat Capital archive and tape

entries.h: July's flat one-carat index hid a 1.7% gain in K to M colours
entries.t: Rapaport's Diamond Pulse for August 2026 published a colour-band breakdown of July's one-carat polished moves. One-carat goods in D to F and G to J colour, in IF to VVS and VS clarity, averaged a gain of 0.1% in July. K to M colours averaged a gain of 1.7%. K to M goods in VS clarity swung from a 0.1% loss to a 2.8% gain. This paper led its edition of 4 August 2026 on the finding that the RapNet Diamond Index for one-carat polished was unchanged across July, closing a slide that had run without a positive print since June 2025, alongside gains of 1.6% for 0.30-carat goods, 1.8% for 0.50-carat goods and 0.2% for 3-carat goods. The colour breakdown shows that the flat headline is an average of a near-flat top and a rising bottom, and that the recovery this paper has described as bottom-up since 14 July 2026 is running from the bottom of the colour scale as well as the bottom of the size chart. The ratio between the two bands is seventeen times, this desk's division of 1.7 by 0.1. The finding rests on a single source, and that source is the owner of the index reporting on its own index; there is no second publisher of RapNet colour-band moves against which to check it. The remaining figures in the same newsletter are already in this paper: global rough production down 8% to 98.8 million carats in 2025 was published here on 27 July 2026, De Beers' first-half revenue down 19% to $1.58 billion on 31 July 2026, and the Section 301 tariff bands of 10% and 12.5% on jewellery and gemstone imports on 25 July 2026.
entries.s: Rapaport Diamond Pulse, August 2026 / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Two published references priced the same one-carat lab-grown diamond $61 apart
entries.t: On 11 August 2026 this desk read two public reference pages for a one-carat lab-grown diamond at the same hour. CaratRadar, republished that day, put the one-carat average at $711 and states on the page that its figures are asking-price averages by shape, carat, colour and clarity, calculated from active certified listings across major online retailers and refreshed daily. TheDiamondPrice, carrying an August 2026 date, put the fair market price of a one-carat round at $650, said most comparable stones sit between $590 and $760, and gave its benchmark as E to F colour and VVS clarity. The difference is $61, or 9.4% of the lower figure, derived by this desk. The two readings are not irreconcilable: the $711 asking average sits inside the $590 to $760 band the second page publishes, above its $675 midpoint, which is where an offer should sit relative to an estimate of transaction value. Neither page publishes the ask-to-sale distance as a number. This paper carried a third reference, StoneAlgo at $511 dated 7 August 2026, in its wire on 9 August; that page was not re-read on 11 August. Across the three, the published span for the same stone is about 39%. Lab-grown took 61% of United States engagement centre stones in 2025, a figure this paper published on 30 July 2026. This paper carries two lab-grown one-carat marks of its own and they differ: the newsroom tape carries $711, the CaratRadar asking-price average read on 11 August, while the site's tape chip carries $475, the midpoint of the published CVD wholesale band dated 30 July 2026 and locked by the build to the lab-grown price list it links to. Both are footnoted on the page with their quantity and date. A third figure of $727 was printed on the retail desk panel under the label "Lab-grown 1ct, wholesale" with no source or date attached, disagreeing with this paper's own wholesale midpoint under nearly the same label; it was removed on 11 August 2026 and replaced with the sourced $475. The RapNet Diamond Index and the Zimnisky rough index returned no numeric reading for a seventh consecutive session and both carry unreachable.
entries.s: CaratRadar / TheDiamondPrice / Carat Capital archive and tape

entries.h: The Dubai gap holds at AED 10.44 as all three readings move together
entries.t: On 11 August 2026 Kitco's live board at 06:00 New York time put gold at $4,372.80 an ounce, which is $140.59 a gram at 31.1035 grams to the troy ounce and AED 516.31 a gram at the dirham's fixed peg of 3.6725 to the dollar; both conversions are this desk's arithmetic and are published by no source. LivePriceOfGold's Dubai board, timestamped 11 August at 10:04 UTC, read AED 516.26 a gram for 24-carat gold, five fils from the peg figure and about one hundredth of one per cent away. Goodreturns' Dubai page, dated the same day, read AED 526.75 for 24-carat and AED 487.75 for 22-carat. The difference between the counter page and the peg arithmetic is AED 10.44 a gram, or 2.02% of the metal, against AED 10.66 on 10 August and AED 1.08 on 7 August, all three derived by this desk. Overnight the three readings moved almost in lockstep: the peg figure added AED 3.72, LivePriceOfGold AED 3.81 and Goodreturns AED 3.50, a spread of AED 0.31 across the three. That resolves the open question left by this paper's 10 August lead. The AED 13.25 step Goodreturns took between 7 and 8 August was a single repricing rather than a page that had stopped updating, and the margin it opened has since held through a rising metal. Under the one-price rule the tape carries the Editor's 06:00 press-time reading, written back over the 04:58 mark of $4,369.70, $64.60, $1,752.00 and $1,357.00: gold $4,372.80, silver $64.79, platinum $1,764.00 and palladium $1,362.00. Measured against this paper's own mark of record 24 hours earlier those are gains of 0.72%, 1.25%, 1.55% and 1.64%; Kitco's own session line at the same moment read gold and silver lower against its previous close, which is two conventions rather than two prices. The gold-to-silver ratio narrows to 67.49 from 67.84.
entries.s: Kitco / LivePriceOfGold / Goodreturns / Carat Capital arithmetic at the AED peg

entries.h: Kalyan Jewellers launches a Tamil Nadu-only banner, to be grown by franchise
entries.t: Kalyan Jewellers announced on 3 August 2026 the launch of Akshaya Thanga Maligai, a second retail brand intended to trade only in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The first showroom opens at Panagal Park in T. Nagar, Chennai, on 21 August 2026, selling hallmarked gold and certified diamond jewellery designed to regional preferences. The company has said it will expand the brand within Tamil Nadu through a franchise model before considering any other state, and has appointed the actor Sivakarthikeyan to support its visibility. Rajesh Kalyanaraman, executive director, framed the reasoning as regional markets offering significant long-term growth opportunities when approached with a truly local proposition. Kalyan Jewellers itself operates more than 400 showrooms across India, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, the United States and the United Kingdom. No investment figure was disclosed. The choice of franchising rather than owned showrooms places the working capital for the gold inventory on franchisee balance sheets at a point when gold spot stood at $4,372.80 an ounce on this paper's tape the same morning. The demand backdrop previously filed by this paper is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter of 2026 to 75.1 tonnes, its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, with the value of that demand up about 50%, and Kalyan taking more than 46% of its June-quarter revenue in recycled metal and more than 55% in the month of June alone.
entries.s: The Retail Jeweller (3 August 2026) / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Two Dubai gold pages read 2.11% apart on the same morning, and neither is wrong
entries.t: On 10 August 2026 two of the most widely quoted Dubai gold pages published materially different rates for the same metal on the same day. LivePriceOfGold's Dubai board, timestamped 10 August at 10:07 UTC, read AED 512.45 a gram for 24-carat gold, AED 470.43 for 22-carat, AED 448.40 for 21-carat and AED 384.34 for 18-carat, and states on the page that it prints a raw gold rate to which commission and labour charges are added. Goodreturns' Dubai page, dated the same day, read AED 523.25 for 24-carat and AED 484.50 for 22-carat, reporting no change against 9 August. The gaps are 2.11% on the 24-carat line and 2.99% on the 22-carat line, both derived by this desk from the two published figures. Kitco's live board at 5:57am New York time on 10 August put gold at $4,341.40 an ounce, which is $139.58 a gram at 31.1035 grams to the troy ounce and AED 512.59 a gram at the dirham's fixed peg of 3.6725 to the dollar; both conversions are this desk's arithmetic and are published by no source. That places LivePriceOfGold AED 0.14 from the raw-metal figure and Goodreturns AED 10.66 above it. Goodreturns' own ten-day table runs AED 485.25 on 1 August, 487.25 on the 2nd and 3rd, 485.50 on the 4th, 492.25 on the 5th, 510.25 on the 6th, 510.50 on the 7th, 523.75 on the 8th and 523.25 on the 9th and 10th: a step of AED 13.25 between 7 and 8 August against a metal move of AED 3.13 over the same span, then three flat days while spot continued to move. Read against this, the three UAE readings this paper printed for the 7 August session without choosing between them, Khaleej Times at AED 517.50, one bureau desk at AED 510.25 and another at AED 514.00, sit on two different lanes rather than representing three attempts at one figure; the peg arithmetic for 7 August gives AED 509.42.
entries.s: Kitco / LivePriceOfGold / Goodreturns / Carat Capital arithmetic at the AED peg

entries.h: India hallmarked 5.9 million silver articles in FY2025-26, nearly double the year before
entries.t: The Bureau of Indian Standards disclosed on 9 August 2026 that the volume of hallmarked silver articles in India rose to 5.9 million pieces in the 2025-26 financial year from 3.2 million in 2024-25, an increase of about 84% derived by this desk from the two published counts, and set out a plan to scale up testing and certification capacity to match. The bureau attributes the rise to consumers moving into silver as gold prices have risen beyond reach. About 230 bureau-recognised assaying and hallmarking centres currently handle silver testing across the country. The bureau's recognised laboratory network has grown from 147 in 2014 to 440, and government-empanelled laboratories from 24 to 350, against ten standalone bureau laboratories and roughly 270,000 product samples tested; the bureau holds about 700 mandatory standards out of 23,000 in total. Nishat S Haque, deputy director general for laboratories, said the referral and assay laboratory expansion would run across the next two years. Gold surveillance remains in-house while silver testing is outsourced to the recognised centres as capacity is built. Silver hallmarking has been voluntary in India since 2005 and no timeline has been announced for making it mandatory, so the 5.9 million figure counts articles voluntarily submitted rather than total production. A hallmark unique identification number for silver articles was introduced in September 2025. The demand backdrop previously filed by this paper is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter to 75.1 tonnes, its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, and Kalyan Jewellers taking more than 46% of June-quarter revenue in recycled metal.
entries.s: Bureau of Indian Standards via Business Today, Business Standard and The Daily Pioneer

entries.h: Etsy cuts 220 roles from product and engineering in a quarter it beat
entries.t: Etsy disclosed on 6 August 2026 a restructuring removing approximately 220 roles, about 12% of its marketplace workforce, falling mainly on the product and engineering organisation, at an estimated charge of about $35 million, primarily severance and benefits, to be booked in the third quarter of 2026 and completed within it. Approximately 1,600 employees remain. The company stated that the reduction is not a cost-cutting measure and is not related to artificial intelligence, describing the intent as flatter teams with wider remits, fewer handoffs and quicker decisions. The plan was announced alongside second-quarter results for the period ended 30 June 2026: revenue of $668.3 million, up 6.2% year on year against a FactSet consensus of $646.1 million; gross merchandise sales from continuing operations of $2.58 billion, with Etsy-only gross merchandise sales up 7.5%; a revenue take rate of 25.9%; active sellers up 5.9% to 5.7 million; and active buyers down 0.4% to 87.0 million. The reported net loss of $46.7 million is driven by $161 million of losses on discontinued Depop operations rather than by the core marketplace. Kruti Patel Goyal took the chief executive role earlier in 2026. Wedbush read the reduction as supportive of the gross merchandise sales trend. Jewellery and personal accessories is one of the six largest categories by gross merchandise sales in Etsy's own filings; third-party estimates place it near 30% of the platform total, a figure this desk carries as an outside estimate because Etsy does not publish a category split.
entries.s: Etsy Q2 2026 Form 10-Q / Reuters / Shopifreaks / MarketScreener

entries.h: QVC Group leaves Chapter 11 in 113 days having cut more than $5 billion of debt
entries.t: QVC Group formally emerged from Chapter 11 protection on 7 August 2026, having filed on 16 April 2026, a span of 113 days derived by this desk from the two dates. The restructuring removed more than $5 billion of debt. As part of the exit the company issued $1.2 billion of take-back notes due 2032 carrying a 10% coupon, disclosed in a regulatory filing, and secured a $600 million asset-based lending facility; the equity was approved for trading on Nasdaq under the ticker QVCG. David Rawlinson, chief executive since 2021, stepped down at the exit and was succeeded by Mike George, who previously ran QVC for more than a decade, as interim chief executive officer and board chair with immediate effect, alongside a newly appointed eight-member board. The company entered court with a pre-negotiated restructuring plan intended to compress the timetable, and the plan received judicial approval in July before the exit closed. Fine and fashion jewellery has been among the top-selling categories on the QVC platform, making the outcome directly relevant to suppliers who use long-form television demonstration as a volume channel. Alex Hennick, president and chief executive of A.D. Hennick & Associates, said the company still has brand recognition, loyal customers and strong vendor relationships. The 10% coupon on the new paper is the credit market's price for the business after the debt reduction and is carried here as the material figure alongside the headline cut.

entries.h: Pandora names Paulo Garcia chief financial officer, the third top seat to turn in a year
entries.t: Pandora announced on 6 August 2026 the appointment of Paulo Garcia as chief financial officer. Garcia joins the company on 1 October 2026 and assumes the role on 1 December 2026, succeeding Anders Boyer, who retires on 30 November 2026 after more than fourteen years with the company and remains until 31 March 2027 to support the handover. Garcia is a Portuguese national with twenty-five years of international executive experience across Europe and Latin America. He joins from the chief financial officer's role at Walmart de Mexico y Centroamerica, a separately listed subsidiary with about $50 billion of revenue and 240,000 employees, and was previously chief financial officer for Europe and Indonesia at Ahold Delhaize and before that at Unilever. The appointment completes a turnover of three senior seats inside twelve months at the largest jewellery company in the world by units: Berta de Pablos-Barbier takes office as chief executive on 1 January 2027, and Andre Branch was named president of the North America cluster in an announcement this paper filed on 5 August 2026 as pandora-fills-the-seat. None of the three arrives from the jewellery trade. Pandora's own published figures put the company at around 7,000 points of sale globally including more than 2,800 concept stores, and approximately 39,000 employees. The company sells lab-grown diamonds in eight markets, having added Spain and Italy in June 2026 with flagship stores in Barcelona and Milan.
entries.s: Pandora Group / WWD / FashionUnited / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: A 1983 Garrard 'Conundrum' egg makes £123,500, about five times its metal
entries.t: A 22-carat gold Cadbury's 'Conundrum' egg, named Cuckoo Cuckoo and made by Garrard & Co. of London in 1983, sold for £123,500, about $166,600, at Batemans Auctioneers & Valuers in Stamford, Lincolnshire on 1 August 2026. Forbes reported the result on 8 August and the auction house describes it as a world auction record for a bejewelled egg of its type. The price is close to six times the pre-sale estimate and about eighteen times the £6,500 the egg fetched at its previous appearance; Forbes dates that earlier sale to 2018 while the Batemans catalogue entry for the same lot is dated July 2017, and this paper carries both readings rather than resolving them. Forbes gives the egg at nine ounces of 22-carat gold, engraved and enamelled in translucent green, blue, orange and white with a cat, a weather vane, stars, mice, a castle and a treasure hunter finding a golden egg. At 91.7% fineness that is between about 7.52 and 8.25 troy ounces of pure gold, depending on whether Forbes means troy or avoirdupois ounces, worth roughly $32,600 to $35,800 at the $4,341.30 an ounce this paper's tape carries from Kitco's 5:00pm New York close on 7 August. That metal figure is derived by this desk from the reported weight and fineness and is not published by any source. Corrected 10 August 2026: this entry first carried 323.6 grams and about $41,400 of bullion, taken from a catalogue entry describing the secret thirteenth egg rather than the one that sold, and called the result four times melt; on Forbes's nine ounces it is about five times. The egg was one of twelve individually designed 22-carat eggs commissioned by Cadbury's in 1983 for a nationwide treasure hunt, with Perspex caskets buried across the United Kingdom each holding a clue to one egg; a thirteenth was made in secret. Greg Bateman, managing director at Batemans, called the eggs a fascinating piece of British cultural history.
entries.s: Forbes / Batemans catalogue via the-saleroom / Kitco

entries.h: The PBoC adds 640,000 ounces in July, its largest month since October 2023
entries.t: The People's Bank of China increased its official gold reserves by 640,000 troy ounces, about 19.9 metric tonnes, during July 2026, published with the monthly reserve data on 7 August. Holdings rose to 76.08 million troy ounces at the end of July from 75.44 million at the end of June, roughly 2,366 tonnes against 2,346. It was the twenty-first consecutive month in which the bank reported a purchase and the largest single-month addition since the 740,000 ounces recorded in October 2023. The gold reserve was valued at $306.35 billion against $303.72 billion a month earlier, within total official foreign-exchange assets of $3.419 trillion, up from $3.416 trillion, putting gold at about 8% of the reserve. Set against this paper's reporting of 2 August, which carried World Gold Council figures showing central banks buying 289 tonnes in the second quarter, up 62%, with China taking 33 tonnes across those three months, July alone runs at close to double China's second-quarter monthly pace. The same World Gold Council data put first-half central-bank demand at 345 tonnes, the smallest first half since 2022's 241 tonnes, after a first quarter revised down to 57 tonnes. July was also the month gold closed at $4,041.70, up about half a per cent and its first monthly gain since February, so the increase in pace came into a market that had barely moved. At the $4,341.30 an ounce carried on this paper's tape, 640,000 ounces is worth about $2.78 billion, a figure derived by this desk from the published ounce count rather than reported.
entries.s: PBoC monthly reserve data via The Private Banker and Bloomberg / World Gold Council / Kitco

entries.h: Shanghai brand counters run 348 yuan a gram above the exchange benchmark
entries.t: The Shanghai Gold Exchange's Au99.99 contract traded at 938 yuan a gram on the morning of 8 August 2026, up 7.53 yuan from the previous close. On the same day, Chinese brand counter prices for 24-carat jewellery stood at 1,286 yuan a gram at Chow Tai Fook, 1,285 at Chow Sang Sang, 1,284 at Lukfook, 1,283 at Lao Feng Xiang and Lao Miao, and 1,281 at Zhou Liu Fu — every major brand inside five yuan of the others and roughly 37% above the exchange benchmark, a spread of 348 yuan a gram. The same Mandarin financial-press tally puts the distance from the Shuibei wholesale price in Shenzhen, where most Chinese gold jewellery is made and traded, to the highest brand counter price at 170 yuan a gram. On 6 August the major brands raised counter prices by close to 60 yuan a gram in a single session, as reported by Sina Finance, against a far smaller move in the benchmark, reversing the pattern in which brand list prices lagged the metal. This paper declined to print a Chinese brand-counter figure on 7 August because two independent reads of that day's price stood at 1,240 and 1,297 yuan a gram, the main aggregator returned empty price cells and a second site failed on its certificate; the 8 August table, cross-checked against two independent brand-price trackers, resolves it. The demand backdrop, previously filed by this paper on 7 August, is China Gold Association half-year figures putting gold jewellery consumption at 132.13 tonnes, down 33.88%, against bar and coin demand of 339.34 tonnes, up 28.42%.
entries.s: Tencent News (Mandarin) / Sina Finance / China Gold Association via Carat Capital

entries.h: Swiss exports to Turkey rise 6.9% while the United States falls 14.8% across the half
entries.t: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry figures for the first half of 2026 put exports to Turkey at 165.2 million Swiss francs, up 6.9% from 154.5 million in the first half of 2025 and 145.2 million in 2024, with Turkey the seventeenth largest market for Swiss watches. The figures were carried by the Turkish press on 6 August, sourced to the federation. Worldwide exports for the half came to 12.8 billion francs, down 0.7%, a total this paper filed on 21 July when the federation published it. The federation's country table shows the United States, the largest single market, down 14.8% for the half though still 2.6% ahead across two years; Germany down 10.5%, China down 5.0% and Japan down 1.6%. Against those, India rose 31.5%, Mexico 14.9%, South Korea 6.5%, the United Kingdom 5.8%, Hong Kong 3.3%, Singapore 2.2% and the United Arab Emirates 1.6%. France rose 63.4%, which the federation attributes to a logistics reclassification rather than to demand. By material, watches in precious metals fell 6.5% and steel watches fell 6.5%, while bimetallic models rose 20.0% and other metals rose 14.4%. Mechanical watches priced under 500 francs at export rose 23.8% while the 500 to 3,000 franc band fell 5.7%. Seven million wristwatches shipped across the half, up 2.3% in units, on a wristwatch value of 12.2 billion francs, down 0.6%. Turkey's 165.2 million francs represents about 1.3% of the half's total, a share derived by this desk from the published figures rather than published by the federation. This is the watches desk's first article since 4 August, after four consecutive dark editions.
entries.s: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry / Turkish Minute / Hürriyet Daily News

entries.h: More than 46% of Kalyan's quarterly revenue came in as recycled gold
entries.t: Kalyan Jewellers reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹10,589 crore for the quarter to 30 June 2026, up 46% from ₹7,268 crore a year earlier, and consolidated net profit of ₹349 crore, up 32%. The results were announced on 4 August 2026. Same-store sales in India grew about 28%, international revenue rose 35%, and Candere, the group's digital business, grew 112%. The company operates 524 showrooms worldwide, 354 of them Kalyan-branded in India. The company states that its gold-recirculation campaign, run under the name Shine with India, contributed more than 46% of revenue across the quarter and more than 55% in the month of June alone, reducing its reliance on imported gold. In the same week, MMTC-PAMP, India's only LBMA Good Delivery refiner of gold and silver, launched a limited-edition 10-gram commemorative coin on 4 August struck entirely from 999.9-plus recycled gold, capped at 8,000 pieces in assayer-certified packaging carrying unique identification numbers, unveiled in New Delhi by the Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu. The volume backdrop, previously filed by this paper, is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter to 75.1 tonnes, its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, against a value up about 50%. A 46% revenue rise against a national tonnage down 15% therefore combines a price effect, an exchange effect and a store-count effect; the company's own same-store figure of about 28% is the comparable measure.
entries.s: Business Standard Capital Market / Indian Television / The Tribune

entries.h: P N Gadgil retires Litestyle for YOOU and sets a 100-store target for 2030
entries.t: P N Gadgil Jewellers announced on 8 August 2026 that it has replaced Litestyle by PNG, its lightweight diamond jewellery line, with a new brand called YOOU, offered in 9, 14, 18 and 22-carat gold and positioned for everyday rather than occasion wear. The line currently trades through 13 exclusive brand outlets across Maharashtra and Goa plus shop-in-shop counters across five states, against a stated target of 100 stores by 2030. Sara Tendulkar continues as brand ambassador, carried over from Litestyle. Saurabh Gadgil, chairman and managing director, described the brand as built for contemporary collections and everyday wear. The parent company reported first-quarter revenue of ₹2,413 crore, up 41% year on year, and has said it plans to open roughly 103 stores across its whole portfolio by the end of the current financial year. The segment context previously filed by this paper is that lightweight, low-carat diamond jewellery aimed at everyday wear is the most exposed category to lab-grown substitution: on 7 August this paper reported lab-grown diamond studs selling at $29.99 in the American mall channel. Two Indian jewellers filed news in the same week and both point the same way, Kalyan sourcing more than 46% of revenue from recycled gold and P N Gadgil building a chain around 9 to 18-carat pieces bought without an occasion, both responses to a gold price that has made the traditional heavy-gold Indian purchase unaffordable at the old frequency.

entries.h: July payrolls fall 23,000 against a consensus of 83,000; gold closes at $4,341.30
entries.t: US non-farm payroll employment fell by 23,000 in July 2026 against a market consensus of roughly 83,000 jobs added, a miss of 106,000, with June revised down to a loss of 20,000. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% while the labour force participation rate fell to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years; average hourly earnings rose two cents on the month and annual wage growth slowed to 3.2%. The Bureau of Labor Statistics release page returned HTTP 403 to this desk, and the figures are carried as reported by Brisk Markets and CNBC on 7 August 2026 rather than from the primary release. Kitco's 5:00pm New York close on 7 August had gold bid at $4,341.30 an ounce, up $102.00 or 2.41% against Thursday's close; silver $63.46, up $2.06 or 3.36%; platinum $1,743.00, up $25.00 or 1.46%; palladium $1,357.00, up $4.00 or 0.30%. Fine gold at that level is $139.58 a gram against $138.72 at this paper's Friday morning mark; ten grams of 18-carat gold carries $1,046.85 of metal. Outside sources diverge on the day's gold mark and the divergence is recorded rather than resolved: Trading Economics carried $4,343.43 for 7 August, $2.13 above the Kitco close, and Reuters reporting during the session had spot near $4,356 at its intraday best. This paper carries the Kitco close because it is a stated closing print at a stated time. The CME FedWatch tool had September rate-hike probability at 46% immediately after the release, from 55% before it and against the 56.9% this paper carried on Friday morning. Consumer price data is released the following week. Saturday 8 August is a weekend and spot markets did not trade; the Editor re-read Kitco at press time and the reading matched the 05:00 tape exactly, so the tape stands unamended.
entries.s: Kitco / Brisk Markets / CNBC / Trading Economics

entries.h: Gold added $26.80 after the morning mark while platinum gave back $29.00
entries.t: Carat Capital marked four metals from Kitco spot at 5:58am New York on 7 August, an hour and a half before the payrolls release. Measured against Kitco's 5:00pm close the same day, gold rose a further $26.80 from $4,314.50 to $4,341.30, while silver fell $0.83 from $64.29 to $63.46, platinum fell $29.00 from $1,772.00 to $1,743.00 and palladium fell $25.00 from $1,382.00 to $1,357.00. In session-percentage terms platinum was up 3.14% at the morning mark and closed up 1.46%, surrendering more than half its gain; palladium was up 2.14% and closed up 0.30%; silver was up 4.71% and closed up 3.36%; gold alone improved, from 1.77% to 2.41%. The gold to silver ratio stood at 69.04 on Thursday's close, tightened to 67.11 at the Friday morning mark and widened back to 68.41 at the close. Platinum stood at 41.1% of the gold price in the morning and 40.15% at the close. Measured against this paper's marks of 5 August, the three-session move is gold +$183.00 or +4.40%, silver +$2.16 or +3.52%, palladium +$7.00 or +0.52% and platinum +$2.00 or +0.11%. Both readings are from the same source at two stated times and both were correct when taken.

entries.h: Bonhams sets three Chanel sales for September across New York, Paris and London
entries.t: Bonhams announced on 7 August 2026 a three-city Chanel auction series for September. New York holds Chanel: From the Vault II from 7 to 17 September, led by a gold-tone bird cage minaudière from Virginie Viard's Métiers d'Art Paris-31 rue Cambon collection, set with simulated turquoise and multicoloured crystals, estimated at $20,000 to $30,000; highlights go on view at the house's Manhattan flagship from 17 August. Paris holds Chanel: From the Vault II Paris Edition from 14 to 24 September with roughly 400 lots spanning Karl Lagerfeld's 1990s work to Viard's recent collections, led by a white tweed jacket from the autumn/winter 2025 ready-to-wear collection at €2,000 to €3,000, about $2,300 to $3,460, and including a Lagerfeld-era brooch with rhinestones and turquoise-coloured paste at €700 to €900, about $810 to $1,040. London holds Designer Handbags and Fashion from 21 September to 1 October and carries the heaviest jewellery weighting, with a private collection of Chanel costume pieces from the 1960s to the 1990s led by a filigree snake bangle made by Robert Goossens for Chanel Haute Couture circa 1960, estimated at $13,000 to $20,000, against a pair of Chanel Fine Jewelry Comète Géode earrings from 2024 in 18-carat white gold and diamonds estimated at £2,000 to £3,000, about $2,690 to $4,040. The signed costume bangle therefore carries roughly five times the estimate of the current-production gold and diamond earrings from the same maison, which prices attribution and documentation rather than materials. This is the first substantial auction-house announcement this desk has been able to file in three editions.

entries.h: HKTDC survey of 1,507 puts diamond first on demand and fashion jewellery first on growth
entries.t: The Hong Kong Trade Development Council surveyed 1,507 buyers and exhibitors at its twin fairs, the Hong Kong International Jewellery Show and the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem and Pearl Show, which ran together from 29 July to 2 August 2026 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. On the most-in-demand stone, 29% named diamond, 25% ruby and 20% pearl. On growth potential by segment, 57% named trendy fashion jewellery, 35% precious jewellery and 21% designer jewellery. Yellow gold was named the most popular precious metal by 40% of respondents. Respondents described themselves as cautious about 2026 and said they expect one to two years before confidence is fully restored. Hong Kong's own 2025 trade data provides the base: exports of fine jewellery rose 5%, driven by precious metal prices rather than units; exports of pearls, gemstones and rough diamonds fell 8%; exports of imitation jewellery fell 26%. The twenty-eight-point gap between the fashion jewellery and precious jewellery answers on growth is the widest signal in the survey and sits against a week in which gold closed at $4,341.30 an ounce, $139.58 a gram. Related context previously filed by this paper: China Gold Association half-year figures showing Chinese gold jewellery consumption down 33.88% by weight while bar and coin demand rose 28.42% (7 August).
entries.s: HKTDC via Rapaport / HKTDC Media Room

entries.h: US jewellery value rose 8.6% in the first half on a unit count that fell about 9%
entries.t: Figures from the analytics firm Tenoris, reported by JCK on 5 August 2026, put United States jewellery sales up 8.6% across the first half of 2026 while the average purchase price rose 19% and unit sales declined. June alone rose 13% year on year. Sales of items priced below $1,500 continued to decline. The implied unit change, derived by this desk from the published value and average-price figures rather than published as such, is a fall of roughly 9%. The composition reflects a spending distribution rather than a jewellery-specific trend: The New York Times has the top 10% of American households accounting for nearly half of all consumer spending, and a discretionary category inherits that shape. De Beers chief executive Al Cook, speaking at the JCK show, said larger and higher-quality diamonds are growing in value and desire. The same mechanism appears in three company results previously filed by this paper: Brilliant Earth's second quarter, revenue up 6% on total orders down 2.1% with average order value up 8% to $2,238 (7 August); Richemont's quarter to 30 June, jewellery up 24% within total sales up 20% and a seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit jewellery growth (15 July); and Luk Fook's record profit taken from fixed-price design rather than gram weight (5 August). The Knot separately reports six of ten brides in 2025 chose lab-grown centre stones.
entries.s: Tenoris via JCK / New York Times / company results

entries.h: NY Now closes its first show under Rockview with buyers up 5% and 96% rebooked
entries.t: NY Now's summer market ran from 2 to 4 August 2026 at the Jacob K. Javits Center in New York with 460 exhibitors, more than 70 of them new to the show or returning after an absence, across its Gift and Lifestyle, Jewelry and Accessories, and Home sections. Buyer attendance rose 5% on the previous summer edition. Organisers report a 96% renewal rate for the winter 2027 market and say 107 prospective exhibitors walked the summer floor to assess taking space. It was the first edition under Rockview Management Group, which acquired NY Now and JA New York from Emerald before that company's own acquisition by Apollo, and which has placed the industry veteran Dorothy Belshaw in charge. The winter 2027 market is scheduled for 31 January to 2 February 2027. Neither the attendance rise nor the renewal rate is broken out by section, so the jewellery-specific read is limited: NY Now is a gift and home market with a jewellery and accessories hall inside it rather than a jewellery fair. This paper filed the show's opening on 2 August. Separately and not filed as an article: Etsy is cutting 220 jobs, 12% of its workforce, in product and engineering, with second-quarter sales up 6% and first-half revenue up 5%; no jewellery-seller-specific impact has been reported and it is carried here as context only.
entries.s: Gifts & Decorative Accessories / National Jeweler / NY NOW

entries.h: India's lower house passes a fifteen-year tax exemption for foreign rough sellers
entries.t: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 passed the Lok Sabha on 6 August 2026, proposing an income-tax exemption for qualifying non-resident companies selling rough diamonds in India between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2041, a fifteen-year window. The exemption is conditional on the sale taking place inside a Special Notified Zone; the two relevant zones sit inside the Bharat Diamond Bourse in Mumbai and the Surat Diamond Bourse. The class of qualifying seller covers miners, brokers, aggregators, auction operators and sightholders, and a qualifying company must furnish information when required. The existing regime offers a safe harbour presuming taxable profit at 1.25% of gross revenue, with Indian corporate tax at rates reaching about 33% of profit where the safe harbour is not elected. The stated policy aim is to reduce the movement of rough and encourage direct sales within India, positioning Mumbai and Surat against Dubai and Antwerp. The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council welcomed the introduction. The Bill has cleared the lower house only and requires Rajya Sabha passage and presidential assent before any exemption takes effect; no date has been set for a hearing in the upper house, which makes the 1 October start date an intention rather than a commitment. For comparison, this paper reported on 2 August that a single tender cleared at 100% in Dubai against 75% in Johannesburg, and on 15 July that Dubai's diamond trade was worth $41.7 billion in a year.
entries.s: Rapaport / IDEX Online / GJEPC via Mines to Market

entries.h: All four metals rise on a fifth session, silver up 4.71% into the payrolls print
entries.t: At 5:58am New York time on 7 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,314.50 an ounce, up $75.20 or 1.77% against Thursday's close, a fifth consecutive advance and above the seven-week high carried the previous day. Silver was bid at $64.29, up $2.89 or 4.71%, the largest single-session move of the four; platinum at $1,772.00, up $54.00 or 3.14%; palladium at $1,382.00, up $29.00 or 2.14%. The gold to silver ratio tightened to 67.1 from 69.3, more than reversing Thursday's widening. Against the 6:03am mark this paper carried on 6 August, gold added $43.60 an ounce or 1.02% and silver $2.62 or 4.25% in twenty-four hours. Fine gold at $4,314.50 an ounce is $138.72 a gram against $137.31 the previous session; platinum stood at 41.1% of the gold price against 41.0%. This desk wrote on 6 August that silver turning red beneath a gold high was the clearest internal warning the tape had printed all week; silver reversed that decline in full the following session, and the call is recorded here against the print that followed it. Context: Iran said it had reached an understanding with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, describing it as a temporary route and not a full reopening; ADP put July private hiring at 44,000 against about 50,000 expected, JOLTS was softer and initial claims rose to 199,000; the CME FedWatch tool showed September at 56.9% against 63.4% a week earlier. July non-farm payrolls were scheduled for 8:30am on 7 August, after this edition closed. Two divergences are recorded rather than resolved: this paper's own overnight tape read gold at $4,304.40 at 4:58am, $10.10 below the 5:58am bid, with silver at $64.16 and platinum at $1,763.00 and palladium identical at $1,382.00 on matching previous closes; and Dubai 24-carat retail was quoted at AED 517.50 a gram by Khaleej Times on 7 August, AED 510.25 by this paper's metals desk the same day and AED 514.00 by the overnight desk on 6 August. NAT1 and LGD1 were carried unchanged, the lab-grown reference holding at $709 on CaratRadar for a third straight day against $536 on StoneAlgo, a spread of roughly 24%.

entries.h: China Gold Association puts first-half jewellery down 33.88% and bars up 28.42%
entries.t: China Gold Association half-year figures, reported 6-7 August 2026, put national gold consumption at 511.41 tonnes for the first half of 2026, up 1.23% year on year. Gold jewellery consumption fell 33.88% to 132.13 tonnes while gold bar and coin consumption rose 28.42% to 339.34 tonnes, making investment metal roughly two and a half times the jewellery figure. The association attributes the divergence to elevated and volatile gold prices and to the rollout of new domestic gold tax policies, with temporary price corrections boosting bar sales through banks. These figures sit alongside, and do not match, the World Gold Council data this paper filed on 3 August, which put Chinese jewellery demand at roughly 136 tonnes across the half, a fall of about 30%, and the second quarter at 50.0 tonnes, the weakest since 2004. The gap between the two authorities is about four tonnes and nearly four percentage points, arising from differing definitions between a consumption series and a demand series; both are printed here and neither is preferred. Related context previously filed by this paper: Indian jewellery demand of 75.1 tonnes in the second quarter, down 15% by weight and up about 50% by value (31 July), and Luk Fook's record profit driven by fixed-price design rather than gram weight (5 August).
entries.s: China Gold Association via China.org.cn / China Daily / World Gold Council

entries.h: Brilliant Earth returns to profit on a bigger ticket and fewer orders
entries.t: Brilliant Earth reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $115.1 million, up 6% year on year, on a 2.1% decline in total orders, with average order value up 8% to $2,238. Net income was $0.8 million against a net loss of $1.1 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Gross margin was 57.9%, a 360 basis point sequential improvement. Fine jewellery bookings grew 32% year on year. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $459 million to $462 million and guided the third quarter to roughly flat sales with adjusted EBITDA between $3 million and $5 million. The composition is the result: revenue growth came from ticket rather than customer count, which concentrates the quarter in existing higher-income demand and leaves no volume growth underneath to absorb a trim in that cohort. The pattern matches other results filed by this paper in the same period, including US jewellery revenue rising while tonnage fell (3 August) and Luk Fook's fixed-price mix carrying a record profit (5 August).

entries.h: WPIC's 14% Chinese platinum jewellery decline is a base effect, not a demand fall
entries.t: The World Platinum Investment Council projects Chinese platinum jewellery demand down 14% year on year in 2026 and global platinum jewellery demand down about 6%. The council attributes the Chinese figure to an unrepeated and exceptionally high stock build in the second quarter of 2025, when Chinese fabricators bought platinum ahead of a gold price that had made their usual metal unaffordable; excluding that atypical inventory build, Chinese platinum jewellery fabrication would show a small year-on-year increase. The global 6% contraction reflects North American and European growth consolidating after strong years and Indian demand facing tariff-related headwinds, with the largest single contributor being the Chinese comparison. WPIC separately forecasts a fourth consecutive annual platinum market deficit for 2026, with supply falling short of demand by 297,000 ounces. Against this, platinum spot was bid at $1,772.00 an ounce at 5:58am New York on 7 August, up 3.14% on the session and standing at 41.1% of the gold price. The general caution applies beyond platinum: any 2026 comparison against 2025 in this trade is a comparison against a year in which buyers front-ran the gold price.
entries.s: World Platinum Investment Council via CME Group / WPIC press release / Kitco

entries.h: Claire's puts lab-grown diamond studs on a $29.99 piercing counter
entries.t: Claire's is relaunching its in-store piercing experience across the United States and Canada from August 2026, the second overhaul of that service in three years, and has expanded the starter stud assortment to include lab-grown diamonds and coloured gemstones alongside existing gold and steel options. Piercing kits start at $29.99 with the piercing itself free on kit purchase. The lab-grown range includes 14-carat white gold studs at 0.10 carats total weight, sold as complete kits with aftercare solution. The significance is the price tier rather than the material: at this level grown diamond functions as a finish and hypoallergenic setting specification rather than as a gemstone purchase, and the competitive displacement falls on cubic zirconia and surgical steel rather than on natural diamond. It is the clearest published evidence to date of grown material reaching mass-market starter pricing, and follows this paper's earlier coverage of grown wholesale price declines and of retailers tiering their floors between lab-grown for everyday and natural for rarity.
entries.s: National Jeweler / Forbes / Retail Dive / Claire's

entries.h: Gold makes a seven-week high on a fourth session up while silver turns lower
entries.t: At 6:03am New York time on 6 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,270.90 an ounce, up $24.70 or 0.58% against Wednesday's close and its highest level in seven weeks, a fourth consecutive advance. Platinum was bid at $1,753.00, up $23.00 or 1.33%, and palladium at $1,367.00, up $20.00 or 1.48%. Silver was bid at $61.67, down $0.25 or 0.41%, the only one of the four lower on the session, after leading the complex all week with gains of 3.27% on 5 August and 3.2% the session before. The gold to silver ratio widened back to 69.3 from 67.8, undoing two sessions of tightening. Against the 5:58am mark this paper carried on 5 August, $4,157.80, gold added $113.10 an ounce or 2.72% in twenty-four hours. Fine gold at $4,270.90 an ounce is $137.31 a gram against $133.68 the previous session and $130.17 on 4 August; platinum stood at 41.0% of the gold price, down from 42.0%. This paper's own overnight tape recorded gold at $4,276.60 at 4:58am, $5.70 above the 6:03am bid carried here, and read silver as flat at $61.92 rather than down, a divergence recorded rather than resolved. NAT1 and LGD1 were both carried unchanged; the lab-grown reference was not printed as a market because two trackers stood 28% apart at $709 and $555. July non-farm payrolls are released at 8:30am on 7 August, the first full read on American hiring since the Federal Reserve held on 29 July with three dissents; June's print was 57,000.

entries.h: Alrosa swings to a half-year loss and prepares to idle open pits
entries.t: Alrosa's first-half 2026 accounts, as reported in English-language coverage of the filing, show revenue of 74.2 billion roubles, about $932.5 million, down 36% year on year, and a net loss of 10.67 billion roubles, about $134.1 million, against a net profit of 39 billion roubles, about $490.1 million, in the first half of 2025. Cost of sales fell 20% to 69.5 billion roubles, about $873.4 million, so revenue fell nearly twice as fast as the cost of production. The comparative half carried about 53.1 billion roubles, some $667.3 million, of non-operating income, including roughly 30 billion roubles, about $377 million, from the sale of Alrosa's stake in Angola's Catoca venture, which flatters the base. The company is preparing to place several open-pit mines into care and maintenance during 2026 and has suspended mining at Severalmaz, which accounts for roughly 10% of Russian diamond output. The 2026 production target of 25 to 26 million carats, down 14% from 29.7 million carats in 2025, is not new: it was set out by the company's head in December 2025, with the stated reason that it was not a question of capacity but of regulating demand and global inventories. For comparison, De Beers' consolidated average realised price fell 32% to $105 a carat across the same half, filed by this paper on 31 July. These figures rest on a single English-language report of the filing and no second outlet has yet carried them.
entries.s: Sada Elbalad / Interfax (Dec 2025) / De Beers Group

entries.h: Signet gives Blue Nile to a Tiffany merchandising veteran
entries.t: Signet announced on 5 August that Pam Cloud becomes president of Blue Nile effective 10 August, reporting to Joan Hilson, Signet's chief operating and financial officer. Cloud has more than thirty years in luxury retail, of which more than twenty-five were spent at Tiffany and Co., latterly as senior vice president and chief merchandising officer and a member of the executive committee. She subsequently founded Roseate Jewelry, a direct-to-consumer pearl brand. Signet acquired Blue Nile in 2022 for $360 million. The appointment places a merchant rather than a marketer in charge of a business originally built on price transparency for loose stones, which reads as a decision about assortment and presentation rather than traffic or conversion. It is the second senior jewellery appointment in a week and close to the inverse of the first: Pandora named Andre Branch, a consumer-brands executive with no jewellery background, president of its North America cluster from 15 August, filed by this paper on 5 August. Both new presidents start in mid-August, with the American fourth quarter already substantially bought.

entries.h: British buy-now-pay-later came under FCA supervision on 15 July
entries.t: Deferred payment credit, the interest-free instalment model underpinning buy-now-pay-later, entered the United Kingdom's regulatory perimeter under Financial Conduct Authority supervision on 15 July 2026. The market grew from about £60 million of transaction value in 2017 to more than £13 billion in 2024, with the FCA putting British usage at around 11 million consumers. Lenders entering deferred payment credit agreements must be authorised for the relevant consumer credit activities or hold temporary permission under the temporary permissions regime, and must carry out proportionate affordability checks before extending credit and give consumers clear upfront terms covering payment dates, amounts and the consequence of a missed payment. Consumers gain access to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Firms could register for temporary permission between 15 May and 1 July 2026 and have six months from commencement to apply for full authorisation. The relevance to jewellery is direct: most independents accept a provider's checkout plug-in rather than lending themselves, so the authorisation duty sits with the provider, but the January authorisation deadline is the point at which some smaller providers may withdraw. This is a three-week-old rule change filed now for its forward consequences, not news of the day.
entries.s: Financial Conduct Authority / GOV.UK / Reed Smith

entries.h: Onyx Partners bids $934 million for 117 J.C. Penney anchor stores
entries.t: Onyx Partners, a Boston-area private equity firm, has offered $934 million for a portfolio of 117 J.C. Penney stores covering 15.7 million square feet across 35 states, about $8 million a store or roughly $59 a square foot. It is the firm's second attempt; a higher offer of $947 million was rejected in December. Onyx states that financing is fully in place and that it is prepared to close on 25 September. The seller is Copper Property CTL Pass Through Trust, a Jersey City vehicle created after J.C. Penney's 2020 Chapter 11 filing with a mandate to liquidate real estate for the benefit of investors. The relevance to the jewellery trade is the anchor position: J.C. Penney has operated fine jewellery departments for decades, and anchor ownership determines footfall past every specialist jeweller in a mall concourse. An implied price near land-and-shell levels rather than going-concern retail levels indicates a market clearing anchor space on the assumption the current use may not be the final use. The transaction has not closed.

entries.h: Two thirds of American shoppers used an AI chatbot to shop in the past three months
entries.t: Attentive's holiday research, conducted online among 600 United States adults and published in the first week of August 2026, finds that 67% of respondents used an AI chatbot such as ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity to assist with shopping in the previous three months, rising to 80% among Gen Z respondents. Among AI users the most common activities were researching specific products, comparing brands and features, seeking recommendations and finding deals, with 51% using the tools to compare brands and almost three in five asking questions about specific products. On timing, 62% of consumers will plan holiday purchases before November, 71% expect to start shopping before Black Friday, and 46% plan to begin holiday shopping before November. Two limits belong on the figures: a sample of 600 adults surveyed online is small and skews toward respondents comfortable answering on a screen, the same population most likely to have tried a chatbot, and the survey measures consultation rather than conversion, with no figure establishing that a purchase was completed through a model. Related: the Natural Diamond Council has engaged the agency Artefact on how natural diamonds appear inside large language models, filed by this paper on 5 August.
entries.s: JCK / Global Toy News / Retail Dive

entries.h: Every precious metal rises for a third session as gold adds $109 an ounce in a day
entries.t: At 5:58am New York time on 5 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,157.80 an ounce, up $81.20 or 1.99% against Tuesday's close; silver $61.35, up $1.94 or 3.27%; platinum $1,747.00, up $19.00 or 1.10%; and palladium $1,355.00, up $26.00 or 1.96%. It was the third consecutive session in which all four rose. Against the $4,048.80 print this paper carried on 4 August, gold added about $109 an ounce in twenty-four hours. The gold to silver ratio tightened to 67.8 from about 69.0 and platinum stood at 42.0% of the gold price; fine gold at $4,157.80 an ounce is $133.68 a gram against $130.17 the previous session. The move followed reports that the United States, Iran and Oman were closing on an interim agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with an announcement targeted for Wednesday; lower oil cut the inflation path and traders trimmed the odds of a September Federal Reserve increase to about 57% from about 67% a day earlier. Intraday prints were materially higher than the mark carried here, at $4,170.90 at 3:08am and $4,174.70 at 2:44am. Trading Economics printed platinum at $1,760.10 and palladium at $1,372.00, spreads of $13.10 and $17.00 against Kitco, which remains this paper's designated source. NAT1 and LGD1 both carried unchanged; the lab-grown reference was not printed because two trackers stood 28% apart, at $709 and $552, on the same week.

entries.h: Indian futures rise with the global bid rather than behind it
entries.t: October 2026 gold futures on India's Multi Commodity Exchange traded at ₹1,45,359 per 10 grams on 5 August, up ₹1,060 or 0.73%, and September 2026 silver at ₹2,24,109 a kilogram, up ₹2,494 or 1.13%. The same gold contract held above ₹1,43,500 in the previous session. ₹1,45,359 per 10 grams is ₹14,536 a gram of futures-grade metal, a duty-inclusive domestic price that cannot be compared directly with the $133.68 a gram international spot mark. Context: Indian jewellery demand fell 19% in the first quarter and to 75.1 tonnes in the second from 88.8 tonnes, a 15% fall, on World Gold Council figures filed by this paper on 31 July, with the council reporting demand beginning to recover in late June after a month-long lull. Chinese gold jewellery demand fell 28% in the same quarter to 50 tonnes, the weakest since 2004. Third-quarter Indian tonnage will not be published for months; the futures print is a price expectation, not an offtake figure.

entries.h: Hong Kong hard luxury grows four times faster than the city's retail market in June
entries.t: Hong Kong sales of jewellery, watches, clocks and valuable gifts reached HK$5.49 billion, about $699.9 million, in June 2026, up 20% year on year, on Census and Statistics Department figures published 4 August. Total retail sales across all categories were HK$31.49 billion, about $4.02 billion, up 5%, making hard luxury 17.4% of the city's retail spend and marking a fourteenth consecutive month of overall retail growth. Across the first half, jewellery, watches and clocks took HK$31.07 billion, about $3.96 billion, up 25%, against HK$203 billion, about $25.88 billion, up 10%, for all retail categories. The government attributed the run to continued economic expansion, rising local incomes and a steady increase in inbound visitors. The value line is flattered by a record gold price in a market that sells substantial volumes of gold by weight; Luk Fook's June quarter, filed by this paper on 21 July, showed retail value up 32% and gold same-store sales up 50% while diamond same-store sales fell 17% group-wide and 58% on the mainland.
entries.s: Census and Statistics Department via Rapaport / Xinhua / SCMP

entries.h: Pandora fills a six-month North American vacancy with a beauty executive
entries.t: Pandora appointed André Branch president of its North America cluster, effective 15 August 2026, succeeding Luciano Rodembusch, who left in February, leaving the seat vacant roughly six months. Branch joins from the chief executive's role at R.E.M. Beauty and previously held senior positions at Estée Lauder, L'Oréal, Diageo and Kraft Heinz across two decades in consumer brands; he has no jewellery background. Pandora describes North America as one of its largest and most important growth markets and states the brief as strengthening customer engagement, expanding reach and unlocking growth. The appointment follows a wider set of executive changes at Pandora North America reported earlier in the year. The American fourth quarter is already substantially bought by the time he starts.

entries.h: Luk Fook's record year was built on fixed-price jewellery, not on the gold price alone
entries.t: Luk Fook Holdings reported net profit up 88.7% to HK$2.015 billion for the year to 31 March 2026, its highest on record, on revenue up 29% to HK$17.21 billion, with gross profit up 42.9% to HK$6.31 billion and a gross margin of 36.7%. The results were disclosed in late June. The driver, stated in the Chinese-language financial press and largely absent from English pickups, is the pricing mix: sales of fixed-price jewellery, priced by the piece, rose 50.5%, while sales of gold and platinum products priced by weight rose 22%. Weight-priced goods pass the metal cost to the customer and earn the retailer a labour charge; fixed-price goods carry the margin inside the ticket, which protects gross margin when gold is at a record but caps revenue upside when volume returns and moves the price exposure onto the buying and hedging desk. This paper filed the same company's June quarter on 21 July, retail value up 32% and gold same-store sales up 50%, and its split on 22 July, diamond same-store sales down 58% on the mainland.

entries.h: The Natural Diamond Council puts 80% of its advertising behind consumers and inscribes a trust mark
entries.t: Natural Diamond Council chief executive Amber Pepper, speaking at a Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council meeting in Mumbai on Monday 3 August, said at least 80% of the council's advertising spend will be directed at consumers rather than the trade, and that the council's budget is significantly larger than the prior year, without giving a figure. She set out a Diamond Desire Index tracking consideration, purchase intent, sentiment and recommendation in India, China and the United States, with a baseline due September 2026, and a Natural Diamond Mark to be inscribed on natural diamonds and jewellery globally as a consumer trust device. Six transformational pillars were named: industry unity, category marketing, organisation evolution, consumer design, cultural relevance and category protection. The council is working with the agency Artefact on large language model optimisation. Pepper said the trade must stop talking about the crisis and start promoting the desirability of natural diamonds. Context: the RapNet Diamond Index for 1-carat polished was flat in July after thirteen months of decline, and De Beers' consolidated average realised price fell 32% to $105 a carat across the first half.

entries.h: Joopiter opens a standalone watch department with a rolling online sale closing 11 August
entries.t: Joopiter, the digital auction house founded by Pharrell Williams, opened Keeping Measure: Watches and Timepieces, the first sale from the standalone watch department it announced in July under Nate Borgelt, formerly of Bonhams. Lots close on a rolling basis through 11 August. The top lot is an Omega Speedmaster engraved for Alan Bean, the fourth man to walk on the moon, one of thirty examples of the reference produced after the first moon landing and distributed to President Nixon, Vice President Agnew and astronauts of the period; this is number 26, engraved for Bean's command of the 1973 Skylab mission, estimated at $250,000 to $350,000 with bidding at $230,000.
